**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — Section 15, Assignment or Transfer (¶ p0080)**

**What the document says.** Section 15 (located in the run-on miscellaneous block within the Indemnity section, not under its own outline heading) imposes a mutual bar on assignment without the other party's prior written approval, with a single carve-out for "an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate."

**Gaps against the preferred position:**

1. **No M&A/successor carve-out for us.** As drafted, an acquisition of Mortgage Logic.com or a sale of substantially all of its assets would require TrueLink's consent — a consent it could withhold or use as leverage mid-deal.
2. **Unqualified consent standard.** Approval is not subject to a "not unreasonably withheld" limit in either direction.
3. **No competitor bar on TrueLink.** TrueLink could assign the hosting/licensing relationship to one of our competitors, and the affiliate carve-out runs in its favour too.

**What I confirmed absent.** Searches for "change of control", "merger", and "successor" returned no results anywhere in the agreement, so there is no vendor termination or re-pricing trigger on our change of control (the walk-away risk). The redline nonetheless adds a short confirmatory sentence so that a future ownership change cannot be recharacterised as a deemed assignment under Section 15.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** One in-place amendment to Section 15: consent "not unreasonably withheld or delayed"; carve-outs for (a) either party's assignment to a financially responsible affiliate (preserving the existing bargain) and (b) our assignment to a successor by merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all assets/equity; a bar on TrueLink assigning to a Client competitor; and confirmation that a change in our ownership or control is not an assignment and gives TrueLink no termination, suspension or re-pricing right.

**Negotiation note.** The comment offers the fallback — mutual successor assignment on written notice, with consent not unreasonably withheld for other assignments — if TrueLink resists the asymmetry.
